column2: The edition prints تمحض; read تمخض, “labored in giving birth”.
The edition prints أبو حيان and ابن الرفيق, translated as printed; the likely readings are ابن حيان (Ibn Ḥayyān) and ابن الرقيق (Ibn al-Raqīq), as de Slane has.
The edition prints أحيالهم; read أجيالهم, “generations”.
The edition prints المحلين (“those who alight”), translated as printed; the likely reading is المجلين, “those who come first”.
The edition prints الغوائد; read العوائد, “customs”, which the context requires.
The edition prints الإعراب; read الإغراب, “love of the extraordinary”, which the context requires.

The edition prints قبل أفريقش (“before Afrīqish”) of Dhū al-Adhʿār, translated as printed, though the same sentence dates him to the time of Solomon; the likely reading is بعد, “after”, as de Slane has.
The edition prints لأنه بناء خاص (“because it is a particular building”), which says the opposite of what the argument needs; the translation reads “not as a particular building”.
The edition prints الذكاء (“intelligence”), translated as printed; the likely reading is الزكاء, “integrity”.
The edition prints المزني (al-Muzanī), translated as printed; the likely reading is المزي (al-Mizzī).
The edition prints ابن حيان (Ibn Ḥayyān); al-Thiqāt is by Ibn Ḥibbān (ابن حبان), so the translation reads Ibn Ḥibbān.
The edition prints القائل in بهذا الرأي القائل للمستضعفين (translated as printed); the likely reading is الفائل, “feeble”, the word used in introduction.45–46.
The edition prints ستين وأربعمائة (460), translated as printed; al-Qādir reigned 381–422 AH, and de Slane has 402.

The edition repeats the clause إنه لراشد مولاهم قبحهم الله وأبعدهم ما أجهلهم أما يعلمون أن إدريس الأكبر; the second copy reads ما أجلهم (“how great they are”), probably a slip for ما أجهلهم. Both copies are translated.
The edition prints بلخ (Balkh), translated as printed; the sense points to فخ (Fakhkh), as de Slane has.
The edition prints بصدقة (“of a charity”); read بصدقه, “its truth”.
The edition prints فارس (Fārs); read فاس (Fez), the city whose founder Idrīs is named in the same sentence.
The edition prints الكبري; read البكري (al-Bakrī), as “routes and realms” (المسالك والممالك) in the same sentence indicates.
The edition prints براغيين, which is meaningless; read براغبين, “desirous of”, from the context.
The edition prints موضوعة; read موضوعه, “its subject”, as the masculine verb خالف requires.

The edition prints ولم يصل إلينا من فالعلوم كثيرة مما وصل, which is corrupt; the translation gives the sense the context requires, “and it has not reached us — for the sciences are many, more than those that have reached us”.

The edition prints ولا يرفع البراهين الطبيعية حجابا, with no preposition before البراهين; the translation supplies “with”, following de Slane’s sense (“par des arguments puisés dans la nature des choses”).

The edition prints إذ لا يمكن وجوده دون ذلك من بين الحيوانات كلها; a clause seems to have dropped out after ذلك, and an editor’s note records that the Lajnat al-Bayān edition adds ولا يشبهه في ذلك, “and nothing resembles him in that”. Translated as printed.
The edition prints ومنهما (dual); read ومنها, “among them”.
The edition repeats the clause من الزراعة والحصاد والدراس الذي يخرج الحب من غلاف السنبل ويحتاج كل واحد من هذه (the second copy reads الدارس); both copies are translated.

The edition’s sentence is incomplete: the previous row ends إلى غاية (“to an end”) and this row continues وأنه لا بد للبشر من الحكم الوازع; the likely reading is إلى غايته (“to its end”). Translated as printed.
The edition prints وإنما مدركة الشرع; read مدركه, “it is perceived only through the revealed law”.

The edition prints وفيما بين بحر فارس والقلزم وجزيرة العرب (“and between the Persian Gulf and al-Qulzum and the Arabian Peninsula”); the و before جزيرة is read as a slip, so the translation has “between the Persian Gulf and al-Qulzum lies the Arabian Peninsula”.

The edition prints لغيبة الماء (“because of the absence of the water”), which contradicts the argument that the sea covers that region; it is translated as the water’s concealing the land, which is how de Slane takes it.
The edition prints أوليك (Awlīk); the likely reading is أوليل (Awlīl), as de Slane has it.

The words في وسط هذا الإقليم الأول (“in the middle of this first zone”) follow “before it joins the sea” in the edition and may belong with the next sentence (“and on this Nile …”); translated as printed.
The edition prints الصفين; read الصين, “China”, as the sense requires.
The edition prints عذامس; read غدامس, “Ghadāmis”, as the next row has it (غذامس).
The edition prints الجزء الثاني (“the second section”) for the place where the branch passes Dalāṣ; probably the fourth section, as at discussion-2.37. Translated as printed.
The edition prints وصدى وسابور (“Ṣadā, Sābūr”); the Khūzistān town is probably جند يسابور (Jundīshāpūr), as in de Slane. Translated as printed.
The edition prints الحلج; read الخلج, “the Khalaj”.
The edition repeats the clause إلى أن يخرج إلى الجزء التاسع قريبا من شمال هذا الجزء; both copies are translated.
The edition prints آمد (“Āmid”); read آمل, “Āmul”, the Khurāsān town on the Jayḥūn.
The edition prints أسر وشنة (“Asr and Shanna”); possibly أسروشنة (Usrūshana). Translated as printed.
The edition prints يمرها بطا, translated “passes it slowly”; the reading is doubtful.
The edition prints والمغمور (“the flooded”); read والمعمور, “the inhabited”, as the sentence requires.
The edition prints أنطاكية (Antioch) among the coastal towns of the land of the Rūm, though Antioch has been placed in Syria at discussion-2.61; read أنطالية, “Antalya”, as in de Slane.
The edition prints الرافضة (twice); read الرافقة, “al-Rāfiqa”.
The edition prints رمم (“Ramm”); de Slane has Zemm, probably زم (Zamm). Translated as printed.
The edition prints الجوزخان (“al-Jūzkhān”); read الجوزجان, al-Jūzjān, as at discussion-2.52 and in de Slane.
The edition prints وبطرف البحر (“and to the end of the sea”), though the sense points to the Pyrenees mountain, as in de Slane. Translated as printed.
The edition repeats the clause خليج القسطنطينية يخرج من هذا الطرف الجنوبي ويذهب على سمت الشمال; both copies are translated.
The edition prints أردن (“Ardan”); de Slane has Erzen, probably أرزن (Arzan). Translated as printed.
The edition prints الزاب (“al-Zāb”); de Slane has Arran, probably الران. Translated as printed.
The edition prints أطرابزيدة بزيدة (“Aṭrābazīda Bazīda”), which repeats the end of the name. Translated as printed.

The edition prints إلى الجنوب (“to the south”) for the mountain’s course, though it then meets the Encircling Ocean in the north; de Slane has “from the south”, probably من الجنوب. Translated as printed.
The sentence وفي الناحية الجنوبية الغربية من هذا الجزء ويخرج إلى الإقليم السادس من فوقه is incomplete in the edition. Translated as printed.
The edition prints الحرارة العزيزية (“precious heat”); read الغريزية, “innate”, as de Slane does.
The edition prints البلاد الجزيرية (“the Jazīra lands”), both here and in the Egypt sentence; read الجريدية, “the Jarīd lands”, as de Slane has.
The edition prints بعد- أفظارها- (with stray hyphens); أفظارها is a misprint, read أقطارها, “dimensions”, and the translation follows that reading.
The edition prints مدار الأغذية (“the circulation of foods”); the sense points to مضار الأغذية, “the harms of foods”. Translated as printed.
The edition prints بصدقة (“by almsgiving”) twice, in وهو شاهد بصدقة and شاهدة بصدقة; read بصدقه, “to his truthfulness”.
The edition prints عالم القدرة (“the world of power”); the sense points to عالم القردة (“the world of monkeys”), as de Slane has. Translated as printed.
The edition prints الرؤية (“seeing”); read الروية, “reflection”, as in the parallel الفكر والروية in discussion-6.13.
The edition has no negative before نطاق in وهي وجدان كلها نطاق من مبدئها ولا من منتهاها; the translation supplies “no limit” from the context.

The edition prints من أمر اليوم (“of the matter of the day”) and ومعقوبية (not a word); read من أمر النوم (“of the matter of sleep”) and ومعقولية (“intelligibility”), as the following “than for the sleeper” indicates.
The edition prints ربيعة بن مضر (Rabīʿa ibn Muḍar), translated as printed; the likely reading is ربيعة بن نصر (Rabīʿa ibn Naṣr), as de Slane has.
The edition prints ذهاب الاختبار (“the going of testing”); read الاختيار, “choice”, as “as though compelled to speak” requires.
The edition prints الحوكية (translated “al-Ḥawkiyya”); the likely reading is الجوكية (al-Jawkiyya), the yogis.
The edition prints المشتركين (“those who share”); read المشركين, “the polytheists”.

The edition prints ومنها أن هؤلاء البهاليل لا تجد لهم وجهة أصلا (“you find in these simpletons no direction at all”); as a sign distinguishing them from the insane the clause looks incomplete, and de Slane has an unfailing inclination to devotion in the simpletons and none in the insane. Translated as printed.
The edition prints فضائه (“its expanse”); read قضائه, “its judgment”.
The edition prints التحالف (“alliance”); the rule it states (one even and one odd number) points to التخالف, “difference”. Translated as printed.
The edition prints وهي: (اي) for the letter of ten; read (ي), yāʾ.
The edition prints زعد; the abjad values (ز 7, ع 70, ذ 700) require زعذ, as de Slane has. The English reads zʿdh.
The edition prints يستمك (five letters), though the passage says these nine words have two, three or four letters; de Slane has يسقك. Transliterated as printed.
